description: n=40 Solomon category-2 MAIN tier (v3.6): same 12 instances, same families and same train/test buckets as n60_cat2_v1, truncated to n=40. The main tier moved from n=60 to n=40 so that a 12-instance content+admissible matrix is reachable inside the hard 3600 s budget; n=60 becomes the challenge tier.
status: candidate -- the tw_scale column below is the STARTING rung for the v3.6 re-screen, not a measured result. It is written back only after the re-screen reports admissible rows.

protocol.distances: unrounded Euclidean (R-9: exact distances for the main experiment; the §8 red-line anchor uses with_rounded_distances)

admissibility.criterion: CERTIFIED within the work gate, under the v3.6 capped protocol (descent cut at 300,000 LABELS per call with a 120 s non-binding ceiling; certification attempts bounded only by the hard total of 2400+1200=3600 s, at most 3 per run)
admissibility.label_gate_basis: TOTAL labels created in the attempt, including the certification laps
admissibility.why_labels: the wall clock on this machine drifts 1.68x on bit-identical output (935.61 s vs 1573.73 s for 108 iterations and LP_min 397.1891082438668), so admissibility is decided on reproducible work units
admissibility.provisional: the gate value may be adjusted once against the first re-screen batch, with the change recorded in docs/step5-blocker-diagnosis_*.md (the file name carries the latest report timestamp).  `filter_instance_content.py --report --label-gate <X>` re-adjudicates the same JSONL under a new value, so an adjustment costs no re-running

truncation_protocol.why: v3.6 ②/③ as executed and then corrected in §15 of the blocking diagnosis.  The descent handle is a LABEL cap because a time cap decides how much work happens and therefore destroys determinism.  A certification attempt is granted the WHOLE remaining hard total and a label ceiling that cannot bind, because a complete full-network call needs >1200 s and ~1e7-2.5e7 labels on these instances -- bounding it by either the nominal 1200 s or NgRoutePricer's own 3e6 default made certification unreachable (defects P2/P4).  The work gate closes the DESCENT phase only: a certification attempt is not extra search, it is the measurement (defect P3).

split_rule.statement: INHERITED unchanged from n60_cat2_v1: within each family, sort by the measured single-call probe time ascending, then deal alternately into the two buckets with the TEST bucket picking first (ranks 0,2,4... -> test; 1,3... -> train).
split_rule.why: Keeping the assignment identical is what makes an n=40 row comparable to the n=60 row for the same name; re-dealing at n=40 would confound the tier change with a bucket change.
split_rule.side_effect_documented: All three step-5 landing representatives (C201/RC201/R201) fall in the test bucket. That is a consequence of the rule, not a hand-placed exception: each is the cheapest instance of its family, so it is rank 0.
split_rule.tw_scale_source: v3.6 requirement 4: start at x0.8, narrow per rung, floor x0.5. RESET to 0.8 here; the n=60 factors are void both because the instance changed and because they were calibrated under blind pricing.

probe_seconds_VOID: The probe_seconds / probe_labels / probe_cap_frac columns are the n=60 readings carried over UNCHANGED. They are VOID as cost predictions for n=40 and are used for one thing only: ordering the sweep cheapest-first, on the argument already recorded in the filter -- a blind-pricing reading is a lower bound on the honest cost, so it orders without pretending to predict. Nothing in the admissibility verdict reads them.
